summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — ENR.DE +4%, CCH.L +3%, ASML.AS +3%, SMT.L +3%, ASM.AS +2%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (HNR1.DE -4%, MUV2.DE -4%, AAF.L -4%, DHL.DE -4%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: HNR1.DE (-4.37%) — No confirmed news driver found. Hannover Re's Q3 statement is due around now, so the drop may be pre-results de-risking or reinsurance-sector weakness. Unverified. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: HNR1.DE is a large-cap German reinsurer that no strategy lists. A -4.4% drop on a roughly 293 EUR stock also looks like a long-only bot's dip-buy or momentum filters would skip it.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day news found for Siemens Energy. The +3.74% looks like a rebound or AI/power-infrastructure sector move in a high-beta DAX name, possibly ahead of FY results due this week.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ENR.DE is a large-cap German industrial/energy-equipment name, and no uk-eu strategy includes it. A +3.7% move on a ~118 close also sits below typical gap or breakout thresholds.
top_movers.suggestion: Add DAX/Xetra large-caps with 20-day ADV above €100M (such as ENR.DE) to the momentum-trader's uk-eu universe, with the existing breakout filter unchanged. Also add an earnings-calendar flag so names reporting within 3 days are tracked.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-09. Searches turned up only routine treasury-share filings and older results news, so this is likely a sector or defensive-staples rotation move.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CCH.L is a FTSE 100 consumer-staples bottler that no strategy lists. A steady +3.4% move with no gap or volume spike would also fail typical momentum and news-reactive entry filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a low-volatility large-cap staples bucket (FTSE 100 / Stoxx 600 staples) to the uk-eu momentum universe, with a relative-strength-vs-sector trigger (e.g. 1-day move ≥ +3% and ≥ 2× sector median), so non-news sector rotations are caught.

top_movers.catalyst: no obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-09 — likely a sector-wide AI/semiconductor rally in European chip names, following ASML's strong AI-demand commentary at its Q3 results.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ASML.AS is a large-cap Euronext Amsterdam semiconductor-equipment name that no uk-eu strategy includes. A +2.7% sector-beta move would also be too small to trip a gap or momentum trigger.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap EU semis (ASML.AS, STM, IFX.DE) to the momentum-trader universe, gated by a sector-relative-strength rule such as a +2% day with the SOX/Stoxx tech index also up, so sector rallies are caught without single-name noise.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-09. Likely a technical or sector move: growth/tech sentiment lifting a trust whose NAV is driven by private holdings (SpaceX, Anthropic) and US tech.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: SMT.L is a large-cap (~£15bn) closed-end investment trust, not an operating company. A +2.5% move with no earnings or news also fails news-reactive and gap-up filters, and is too mild for momentum screens.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change: a +2.5% drift in an investment trust with no catalyst is within normal range. If wanted, add SMT.L to a UK growth/tech sentiment-proxy watchlist, but don't loosen the momentum gap or volume thresholds for it.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious stock-specific news found; likely a sector-wide rebound in European semiconductor/AI-equipment names (ASML, BESI) after the sharp early-November drop. Could not confirm a driver for 2026-11-09.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ASM International is a ~€30B+ Dutch semiconductor-equipment large cap on Euronext Amsterdam, and no strategy's universe covers it. A +2.4% sector-beta move is also too small to trip typical gap or news-reactive triggers.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a 'EU semicap' basket (ASM.AS, ASML.AS, BESI.AS) to the momentum universe, gated on a basket move ≥ +2% with volume ≥ 1.2× the 20-day average, so sector rebounds can be traded without needing a stock-specific catalyst.

top_movers.catalyst: Probably Endeavour Mining's Q3 2026 results, which an investor calendar lists for 08:00 today. I couldn't find the release or its figures, so this is unconfirmed. A gold-sector move is also possible.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: EDV.L is a FTSE 100 gold miner with a dual TSX listing, and no strategy's universe includes it. A results-day gap at the 08:00 open would also have been missed by pre-market-positioned or post-open momentum filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add FTSE 100 gold/precious-metals miners (EDV.L, FRES.L, etc.) to the uk-eu universe, and release the earnings gate for names that gap up 2% or more on results day within 30 minutes of the open.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed news driver found. Hannover Re's Q3 statement is due around now, so the drop may be pre-results de-risking or reinsurance-sector weakness. Unverified.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: HNR1.DE is a large-cap German reinsurer that no strategy lists. A -4.4% drop on a roughly 293 EUR stock also looks like a long-only bot's dip-buy or momentum filters would skip it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap DAX/MDAX financials, HNR1.DE included, to the news-reactive universe. Gate it on an earnings-calendar flag so results-day gaps of 3% or more get evaluated within the first 30 minutes of the open.

top_movers.catalyst: No clear Nov 9 catalyst found. Munich Re pre-announced strong Q3 and raised its FY26 profit guidance on Oct 23, so this looks like a sell-the-news or sector drop ahead of the Nov 12 final Q3 report.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: MUV2.DE is a large-cap DAX reinsurer that none of the bot's strategies cover. A -4.3% day with no fresh news also wouldn't pass a news-reactive filter.
top_movers.suggestion: (No actionable change: a news-less large-cap insurer drop is not worth adding to a universe, and acting on it would need short capability the bot lacks.)

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed 9 Nov driver found. Likely a continued post-H1 results drift (results 3 Nov: profit +20.5% but fuel-cost and investment pressure) plus Airtel Money IPO and Bharti stake-swap overhang.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: AAF.L is a Jersey/UK-listed, Africa-focused mid-cap telecom, so it isn't in the UK/EU strategy lists. A -4% drift with no fresh catalyst also wouldn't trigger news-reactive or momentum entry filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add AAF.L, or FTSE 100/250 telecoms generally, to the mean-reversion universe. Gate entries on a ≥3% one-day drop with no earnings in the last 5 sessions, so post-results drift can be told apart from catalyst gaps.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-11-09. Q3 results were due about 5 Nov, so this looks like post-earnings drift or a sector/logistics move, and no cause is confirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: DHL.DE is a large-cap German logistics name that no strategy's universe includes. With no news trigger, a -3.9% drift also would not have passed a catalyst or gap filter.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap DAX/STOXX 50 constituents such as DHL.DE to the mean-reversion universe, with a trigger on a one-day drop of at least 3.5% and no earnings event within 2 days.
